_comment: SSOT fixture for tests/test_inversion_scope_preserved.py (PR7/M9). The 14 path:line items the audit measured as BEHAVIOR-changing (not merely cost-changing) if their adjacent explanation is removed during the wave-7 contract-inversion pass. Each 'sentences' entry must survive, whitespace-normalized, verbatim in its file after every commit of the wave and forever after. Two are hang/deadlock risks (ids 1-2); the rest silently destroy a guarantee (mutual exclusion, OOM bound, lease-leak visibility, status-enum authority, blocked_reason groundedness, teardown obligation, base-branch correctness, evidence placement, lead-strand prevention, active-run data safety, red-before-green semantics).

items.hazard: HANG (infinite re-queue) - without the failed-sibling exclusion, decision-table case 2 re-queues a dependent forever
sentences: it will never complete, so a re-queue would loop forever; it falls

items.hazard: DEADLOCK - a barrier gated on a tool-native label the tool never exposes can never release
sentences:
a barrier gated on a
tool-native label the tool does not actually expose (e.g. a literal `blocked` state) is unsatisfiable
and must never be the release condition.

items.hazard: MUTUAL EXCLUSION DESTROYED - the obvious simplification (mkdir -p everywhere) defeats the atomic-mkdir lock
sentences: NEVER `mkdir -p` on the per-module dir - `-p` succeeds on
an already-existing dir and would defeat the mutual exclusion

items.hazard: OOM regression (unbounded-opus-fanout-oom) - an unstated model silently inherits the caller's tier
sentences: never leave `model` unstated "to be safe" - silence is not neutral, it is a hidden opus default.

items.hazard: Lease leak invisible to enforcement - self-provisioning via a sub-agent hides the acquire call from the SubagentStop teardown gate's transcript correlation
sentences:
the SubagentStop
teardown gate correlates a live lease to YOUR dispatch by finding the `allocator.py acquire`
call in YOUR transcript, so provisioning through a sub-agent makes your own leak invisible to it

items.hazard: Status-enum authority confusion - conflating this file's status enum with ODOO-AI-ETHOS #10's different DONE_WITH_CONCERNS field
sentences:
it is NOT the authority for the four-value `status` enum above, which
this file declares in its own right and which diverges from ETHOS #10's own value set

items.hazard: Ungrounded blocked_reason - without the decidability check, a copy-paste-generic blocked_reason passes silently
sentences:
if you could swap in a different module, task, or
caller and the sentence would read equally true unchanged, it names nothing and fails this rule

items.hazard: Browser/instance teardown-rule conflation - three separate clauses prevent (a) an instance-only prohibition being misread onto browser pages, (b) 'advisory enforcement' being misread as 'no obligation', (c) the two teardown tiers being equalized
sentences: not forbid, and never excuses skipping, the browser CLOSE rules below.

You remain contract-bound to close
  every page you opened before DONE; only the ENFORCEMENT tier differs, not the obligation.

Do not equalize them in either direction - tightening browsers to a ledger-block or loosening
  instances to advisory-only breaks this design; the asymmetry is intentional, not an oversight.

items.hazard: Leaf-vs-spawner git-ops confusion - without the agent-launch-capability discriminator, a launched-by-an-agent leaf could be mistaken for a spawner allowed to invoke git-ops
sentences: The discriminator is agent-launch capability, not "was I launched by an agent":

items.hazard: Base-branch defect reintroduced - resolving `base` from the invoking checkout's ambient branch is the exact defect this rule exists to close
sentences:
it MUST NEVER be the value assigned to a `base` / `work-base` /
Repo Capability Card `base` field.

items.hazard: Scattered evidence files - without the family-conditional refusal fallback, playwright/pagecast would write an untracked file with no destination on resolver refusal
sentences:
Both families write by default and neither can be told where; scattering files is
  the defect this rule exists to prevent.

items.hazard: Silent lead-strand - the file's own annotation marks this rationale load-bearing, not narration
sentences:
**Rationale (state it; it is load-bearing, not narration):** in Agent Team mode your plain text and
your written files are invisible to the lead; only `SendMessage` delivers the report.

items.hazard: Active-run data loss - without the mtime-refresh explanation, the destructive orphan-sweep `rm -rf` could be 'simplified' into deleting a still-active run's worklog dir
sentences:
a directory's own
mtime refreshes every time ANY writer appends a new per-writer file inside it, so a still-active
run is never touched

items.hazard: Red-before-green misapplication - without this distinction, a forward-ported test's RED-on-target could be treated as a violation of red-before-green instead of the platform-gap signal it is
sentences: This is **different from red-before-green** (writing a new test that fails first).
